newsitem.title: USA: Carolina Power gets right to control two plants.
newsitem.headline: Carolina Power gets right to control two plants.

text.p: Carolina Power & Light said it has given up an option to buy two independent power plants in return for the right to have dispatch over all five such plants owned by Cogentrix Energy Inc in the utility's service area.

The utility said it will save about $30 million per year in energy costs, or about $175 million over the life of electric power sales agreements contracts reached with Cogentrix in the mid-1980s, which have now been amended.
Under the amended agreements, Carolina Power said, Cogentrix will retain ownership of its facilities.
It will continue to provide process steam to industrial companies under contract to the five plants.

The revised agreements also call for the Cogentrix plants -- located at Lumberton, Elizabethtown, Kenansville, Roxboro and Southport, N.C. -- to be dispatched by CP&L along with other generating plants in order to achieve the most efficient mix of generation sources available.
The five plants have a combined generating capacity of 262,500 kilowatts, CP&L said.
The arrangement extends through 2000 for the Lumberton and Elizabethtown plants, through 2001 for the Kenansville plant and 2002 for the Roxboro and Southport plants, it said.

"The restructuring of the five contracts represents the culmination of over two years of effort by the staffs of Cogentrix and CP&L," said James E. Lewis, executive vice president for operations at privately-owned Cogentrix. "We are also looking for ways to achieve similar success with our projects in Virginia" which suppy power to Dominion Resources Inc's Virginia Power.
The revised agreements became effective September 26, CP&L said. -- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.
